primitives.name: Hip Interposition
primitives.verbatim_quote: 110 FOOTBALL by the opponent in any way, the blocker should endeavor to stop his man by interposing his hips.
primitives.assumptions: Opponent motion is linear; hip orientation aligns with momentum vector.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When opponent velocity exceeds blocker's lateral acceleration capacity.

layer2.mapping: Hip interposition maps to a geometric projection kernel in GSE's spatial exclusion field, where I = cos(θ) represents alignment efficiency.
layer2.telemetry: Angular deviation of opponent trajectory from blocker's axis.

primitives.name: Momentary Suppression
primitives.verbatim_quote: In this, as in blocking, the main purpose rests in so charging the opponent that he is momentarily put out of the play.
primitives.assumptions: Contact impulse is instantaneous; suppression is defined by Δp > threshold.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When F < μmg (frictional limit), suppression fails.

layer2.mapping: Suppression kernel in GSE computes t_s = Δp/F, used to gate opponent influence in next 200ms.
layer2.telemetry: Time window of opponent motion inhibition.

primitives.name: Hole Creation
primitives.verbatim_quote: MAKING HOLES Closely allied to, and in fact almost identical with blocking, is the making of holes in the line, through which to allow the backs to travel toward the opponents' goal.
primitives.assumptions: Lane formation is deterministic; L depends on opponent displacement.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When θ deviates beyond ±π/6 from intended path.

layer2.mapping: Hole creation mirrors a topological cut in GSE's motion graph, where L = v_r × t_s.
layer2.telemetry: Effective lane width at runner's entry point.
